operations.summary: Get additional parameters identities by revision
operations.notes:
Some firewall vendors use special fields in their security policy.
For example: Palo Alto uses Tags, Security Profiles and Log Profiles and Fortinet uses NAT Pools and other NAT configurations.
SecureTrack refers to these fields as "Additional Parameters".
The additional parameters API retrieves the possible values of these fields.
This API is currently supported for Palo Alto Networks firewalls and Fortinet devices managed by Fortimanager.

Fetches list of applications defined in a revision given by ID.
This API is currently supported for Palo Alto Networks firewalls.
In Panorama NG, overrides property in returned ApplicationDTO will be set to true, if the application overrides an original value.
The default value for get_total is false. For API calls that have pagination, set get_total to true on the first call. Use the value to returned in total to determine how many additional calls are required to retrieve all the desired results. To improve performance, omit or set get_total to false on any subsequent calls.

operations.summary: Determine if changes between two revisions are authorized
operations.notes:
This API checks for unauthorized changes between any two versions of a firewall policy.
The API returns authorized if and only if all traffic changes between the two versions were authorized by SecureChange tickets.
The API returns unauthorized if there is at least one change that cannot be matched to a SecureChange ticket.

The API checks access that was granted (checked against access requests with action=Accept) as well as access that was removed (checked against access requests with action=Drop or Remove).
The API returns the authorization status, the relevant tickets in SecureChange and the rules that implement unauthorized access changes.

Note 1: To use this API you must enable "Authorize Revisions with Tickets" in SecureTrack/Configuration/Ticketing.
Note 2: Use the ID returned by the /revisions API for new_version and old_version.
Note 3: The default value for traffic_details and ignore_tickets is false.
Note 4: Traffic that is handled by an implicit rule will not have a rule ID.

parameters.name: traffic_details
parameters.description: Return unauthorized traffic change details for all modified rules

parameters.name: ignore_tickets
parameters.description: Ignore SecureChange tickets and consider all traffic changes unauthorized

responseMessages.message: Change authorization has been successfully calculated
Could not find the requested revisions for comparison

operations.summary: Compare revisions on two different devices in terms of traffic.
operations.notes:
This API compares two arbitrary revisions from any devices. The comparison will be done in terms of allowed/denied traffic.
The API returns authorized if and only if there are no differences between the traffic allowed/denied by the rules in the two revisions.
The API returns unauthorized if there is at least one difference in terms of allowed/denied traffic between the two revisions.
Note 1: To map policies from one revision to the other use oldId2newIdMap and provide the UIDs of the policies to be compared.
Note 2: Parameter in the request body specifies if the result will return traffic difference details for all incompatible rules
Note 3: The format of the result is the same as the one returned by /change_authorization
Note 4: The API accepts in request body only one pair of oldId - newId map
Note 5: The request is valid only if the mapping ids are found in the active policies

parameters.name: body
parameters.description: Request parameter containing the versions of the revisions to be compared and the policy mapping between the revisions.

operations.summary: Get name and status for all change windows
operations.notes:
Retrieves a list of all change windows.
For valid pagination, both start and count should be provided. Otherwise, pagination is turned off.
The default value for get_total is false. For API calls that have pagination, set get_total to true on the first call.
Use the value to returned in total to determine how many additional calls are required to retrieve all the desired results.
To improve performance, omit or set get_total to false on any subsequent calls.

parameters.description: Starting result for query allowable value is numeric

parameters.name: count
parameters.description: Number of change windows for query starting from starting page, allowable type is numeric

parameters.name: get_total
parameters.description: Set to true to get the total number of items that can be retrieved

responseMessages.message: For correct pagination provide a value for the start and count parameters

Count parameter must be a positive value

operations.summary: Create new Internet representation for a device
operations.notes:
The internet referral lets you represent the Internet as an object on a device.
See REST API: /internet_referral/{deviceId:[0-9]+}/object for a description of how internet referral is resolved.

responseMessages.message: Device with given ID does not exist
Internet referral object can only be configured for StoneSoft (except master engine) or Check Point SMC/CMA devices
Internet referral configuration for given device ID already exists

operations.summary: Get resolved Internet representation for device
operations.notes:
The order of precedence used to resolve the Internet object is:
Step 1: Identify the Internet referral:
Search for a defined Internet referral on the specified device.
If it is not found on the device, search the parent and grandparents (up the device tree) for a defined Internet referral.
If a defined Internet referral is found, then match the name in the Internet referral to a network object, as defined in Step 2.
If an Internet referral is not found, it resolves to "Any".
Step 2: Resolve the object by name:
Search the specified device for a defined network object that matches the name returned in Step 1.
If a matching network object is not found, an error will be returned.

the issuing and expiration dates, the customer identifier, name and optionally the site identifier

operations.notes:
Use this API to manually trigger retrieval of topology data collection.
This functionality is applicable to all root devices with dynamic topology setting enabled.
The topology data will be retrieved for the root device and all of its managed devices.
Use /securetrack/api/devices/bulk/tasks/{task_uid} API to track the progress of the retrieval.
After the task status is complete, run Fast Topology Sync to see the updated device topology on the map.

Use this API to delete SecureTrack devices in bulk.
This function is supported for all devices.
The input for API is the Management ID (mgmt_ID).
Use the mgmt_ID of a management device to delete it and its managed devices.
Use multiple mgmt_IDs to delete individual devices in bulk.

Use this API to add a single device or a list of devices to SecureTrack.
The following devices can be added: Check Point CMA R80, SMC R80, Smart 1 Cloud; Cisco ASA; Cisco Router; Cisco Nexus; Cisco XR; Cisco Meraki; Palo Alto Panorama NG; Fortinet FortiManager; Microsoft Azure; Amazon AWS; Arista CVP and EOS
The API body should include a JSON file with the mandatory parameters for the operation.
String parameters contain only lower and upper case letters, digits, space, dot, backward slash, forward slash, underscore or one of the following signs: #@:;=!^().
Currently supported types: CMA, SMC, Smart 1 Cloud, ASA, Cisco Router, Nexus, XR, Cisco Meraki, Panorama NG, FortiManager, Azure, AWS, Arista CVP and EOS

This API verifies connection to the provided device, before adding a device.
This is done by:
  Cisco - Connect with SSH and see that the credentials are correct.
  Check Point (Excluding Smart 1 Cloud) - Test OPSEC connectivity. For R80 devices, this also verifies the connectivity for API login.
  Panorama - Login through the API to check connectivity.
  Fortimanager - Login through the API to check connectivity.
  Arista - The SSL certificate is retrieved.
If the connection test fails the device will not be added.
The connection is not verified for Smart 1 Cloud, Cisco Router,Nexus and XR.
Only "live" device with correct credentials can be added using this API.
For Cisco Router, Nexus and XR there are 2 usage examples : one only with mandatory fields (device name example : Router-Cisco-mandatory-fields) and one with both mandatory and optional fields ( device name example : Router-Cisco-all-fields).
Only for Cisco Router, the 'router_operating_system' field can take the following values: IOS, IOS-XE and IOS-XE-SDWAN. The latter corresponds to Cisco Viptela cEdge routers.

When adding a new AWS or Azure device and the field use_cloud_organization is set to true, than the cloud_organization and account_id or subscription _id fields become mandatory.
The value for cloud_organization must match the name defined in the Cloud Organization settings within TOS.
Only users with Super Admin privileges are authorized to use this setting.
When adding a new Azure subscription using the API, the usage analysis feature will be turned off by default, unless you explicitly specify "collect_rule_usage_traffic_logs" : true and also "collect_object_usage_traffic_logs" : true and also "rule_optimizer_usage" : true. See Azure example body - "azure_device"

Use this API to edit the settings of a management device, including changing multiple parameters in the same call.
The API body should include a JSON file with the mandatory parameters for the operation.
String parameters contain only lower and upper case letters, digits, space, dot, backward slash, forward slash, underscore or one of the following signs: #@:;=!^().
The following devices can be edited: Check Point R80+,Check Point Smart-1, Cisco ASA, Cisco Meraki, Panorama NG, Fortinet FortiManager, Microsoft Azure, Juniper MX and SRX, Amazon AWS, Arista CVP and EOS.
Microsoft Azure (we currently support editing vnet and management device).
Note: This API cannot be used to edit SecureTrack Domains and SecureTrack Servers.
This API verifies connection to the provided device, before updating a device. For Juniper MX only the username and password update is supported. No validation is done for these fields.
For Juniper SRX only the username, password and vault update is supported. Only the vault name is validated.
For the supported devices the validation is done by:
  Cisco - Connect with SSH and see that the credentials are correct.
  Check Point - Test OPSEC connectivity and verifies the connectivity for API login.
  Panorama - Login through the API to check connectivity.
  Fortimanager - Login through the API to check connectivity.
  Arista - The SSL certificate is retrieved.
If the connection test fails the device will not be updated.
Only "live" device with correct credentials can be updated using this API.
Only for Cisco Router, the 'router_operating_system' field can take the following values: IOS, IOS-XE and IOS-XE-SDWAN. The latter corresponds to Cisco Viptela cEdge routers.
When editing an AWS or Azure device and the field use_cloud_organization is set to true, then the field cloud_organization becomes mandatory. Additionally, the account_id or subscription_id fields can no longer be used.

Use this API to import more managed devices to SecureTrack.
The following devices can be added: Device Groups (for Panorama), Administrative Domains (for FortiManager), Account (for Meraki). Currently supported types: Panorama, FortiManager, Cisco ASA, Microsoft Azure, Cisco Meraki, Amazon AWS, Arista Eos.
Please see examples below per device id: device id 1 for Panorama, device 2 for FortiManager, device id 3 for Cisco ASA, device id 4 for Azure, device id 5 for Meraki, device id 6 for Amazon, device id 7 for Arista Eos.

operations.notes:
Fetches list of network objects from specific revision
The default value for get_total is false. For API calls that have pagination, set get_total to true on the first call. Use the value to returned in total to determine how many additional calls are required to retrieve all the desired results. To improve performance, omit or set get_total to false on any subsequent calls.
The show_members parameter is only relevant if type=group.
If type=group, the returned results will also include full details of every group member.
Set show_members=false to return only the name and ID of the members, and omit the full details of the group members.
Each UID in the 'uids' parameter can be given either with or without curly braces ('{}'). In case braces are used, they should be encoded. Example:
Instead of uids={58F8FA19-8A4F-7081-72D8-84ACAFD10D1B}, write uids=%7B58F8FA19-8A4F-7081-72D8-84ACAFD10D1B%7D ('{' encoded to '%7B' and '}' encoded to '%7D')

operations.summary: Get network objects matching specified criteria
operations.notes:
You can search for network objects where the IP address, name or comment fields have a specified text string,
or you can search for network objects that have an IP address that matches, contains or is contained in a specified IP subnet,
or you can search for network objects by uid.
examples:
https://192.168.1.1/securetrack/api/network_objects/search?filter=text&name=Access_Role&identity_awareness=supported ||{
	"network_objects": {
		"count": 1,
		"total": 1,
		"network_object": {
			"@xsi.type": "identityAwarenessDTO",
			"id": 169197,

parameters.name: context
parameters.description: Returns results for the specified domain ID.

parameters.name: start
parameters.description: Returns the results beginning with the specified result number.

parameters.name: count
parameters.description: Returns the specified number of results. If this field is not added or if a number greater than 100 is specified, the query uses "count=100".

parameters.name: filter
parameters.description: "text" filter returns network objects where the IP address, name or comment fields have a specified text string. "subnet" filter returns network objects that have an IP address that matches, contains or is contained in a specified IP subnet. "uid" filter returns network objects with the specified uid. If no filter is specified, the "text" filter is used.

parameters.name: device_id
parameters.description: Returns network objects belonging to the specified device_id.

parameters.name: ip
parameters.description: (For "text" filter) You can specify "ip" to find network objects with the specified text in the IP address field.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: (For "text" filter) You can specify "name" to find network objects with the specified text in the name field.

parameters.name: comment
parameters.description: (For "text" filter) You can specify "comment" to find network objects with the specified text in the comment field.

parameters.name: any_field
parameters.description: (For "text" filter) You can specify "any_field" to find network objects with the specified text in the IP address, name or comment fields.

parameters.name: exact_match
parameters.description: (For "text" filter) You can add "exact_match=true" to find network objects with the specified text in the comment field. If this field is not specified, the query uses "exact_match=false".

parameters.name: contained_in
parameters.description: (For "subnet" filter) You can specify "contained_in" to find network objects that are contained in the specified IP subnet. For example, 10.1.0.0 is contained in 10.0.0.0.

parameters.name: contains
parameters.description: (For "subnet" filter) You can specify "contains" to find network objects that contain the specified IP subnet. For example, 10.0.0.0 contains 10.1.0.0.

parameters.name: exact_subnet
parameters.description: (For "subnet" filter) You can optionally specify "exact_subnet" to find network objects in a desired subnet mask. When not specified, a default mask is calculated according to the subnet class - e.g. 255.255.255.255 for a subnet of 1.1.1.1, 255.255.255.0 or a subnet of 1.1.1.0 etc.

parameters.name: uid
parameters.description: (for "uid" filter) Returns network objects with the specified uid.

parameters.name: identity_awareness
parameters.description: Get access role objects as "identity_awareness" if identity_awareness parameter is "supported". Default type returned is "identity_role"

parameters.name: typeOnDevice
parameters.description: You can specify  "typeOnDevice" to find network object groups that are EDL.

responseMessages.message: The typeOnDevice value is not valid.Use edl_ip_list as value to search EDL groups.

operations.summary: Get generic devices that are configured in ST
operations.notes:
Returns a list of the generic devices included in all the domains that the user has permission to.
Use context and/or name optional parameters to get more specific results.
To get context optional parameter, you can call /domains/ API and use the id included within the returned domain DTO.

operations.summary: Add generic device to Topology model
operations.notes:
Upload a configuration file that will be used to add a generic device to the Topology model.
The context field is the domain ID to which the generic device is added: If not provided, the device is added to the global domain.
configuration_file must include a valid generic device configuration.
The specified path must point to a file on the computer being sue to make the REST API call.
If update update_topology = true, then the Topology model will be updated immediately after the device is added.
For maximum efficiency, if you are adding multiple generic devices in consecutive API calls, you can set update_topology = false on all API calls except for the last one. On the last call, set update_toplogy = true.Default value for update_topology = true.
For more information on input file formats, refer to Knowledge Center topic 'Adding and Updating a Generic Device'.

responseMessages.message: The generic device was created successfully
User is not permitted to access the specified domain

operations.summary: Update an existing generic device in the Topology model
operations.notes:
Modify an existing generic device by uploading a new configuration file and/or specifying a new name.
If name field is specified, the generic device will be renamed.
configuration_file is optional, if provided it must include a valid generic device configuration.
The specified path points to a file in the client machine.
If a generic device name is changed and a new configuration file is not provided, topology will not be synchronized (update_topology flag is ignored).
Default value for update_topology = true.
To save time when there are several consecutive api calls: For the last call, set update_topology = true (for all other calls, update_topology = false).
For more information on input file formats, refer to Knowledge Center topic 'Adding and Updating a Generic Device'.

responseMessages.message: The generic device was updated successfully.
A new name or a new configuration file must be indicated in order to update generic device with id {}
Failed to update generic device with id {}
A 'Generic Device' with the specified ID was not found

operations.summary: Delete generic device from Topology model
operations.notes:
Delete a generic device from the Topology model.
The ID must be for a valid generic device listed in the Topology Model.
If update update_topology = true, then the Topology model will be updated immediately after the device is deleted.
For maximum efficiency, if you are deleting multiple generic devices in consecutive API calls, you can set update_topology = false on all API calls except for the last one. On the last call, set update_toplogy = true.
Default value for update_topology = true.

responseMessages.message: Failed to delete generic device with id {}
A 'Generic Device' with the specified ID was not found

operations.summary: Export configuration file of specific generic device
operations.notes:
Export configuration file of specific generic device.
The ID must be for a valid generic device listed in the Topology Model.

responseMessages.message: Generic device configuration file exported successfully.
Failed to export configuration file of generic device with id {}
User is not permitted to access the specified domain.
Not found configuration file of generic device with id {}.
A generic device with the specified ID was not found

operations.summary: Create or update generic Route Maps
operations.notes:
This API allows creating or updating one or more generic route maps for a specific network device.

Each route map must contain:
- A human-readable `name` (unique identifier for the route map)
- A list of `interfaces` where the route map is applied
- A list of `entries`, where each entry defines policy-based routing behavior

Entry Parameters:

- seq_number: Unique sequence number that defines evaluation order within the route map
- matcher_policy_name: Name of the generic policy that defines traffic matching criteria
- Must reference an existing generic policy created via the generic policy APIs
- See: POST /topology/generic/policy (create policy)
- See: GET /topology/generic/policy (retrieve policies)
- The referenced policy contains rules that define source, destination, service, and action criteria
- entry_action: Action to take when traffic matches the policy ("Accept" or "Deny")
- actions: Array of routing actions to apply when entry matches and is accepted

Routing Action Parameters:

- nexthop: IP address of the next hop router (IPv4/IPv6), e.g. "10.0.0.1""
- Use null if not setting a specific next hop
- interface: Name of the egress interface, e.g. "GigabitEthernet0/1", "FastEthernet0/0"
- Use null if not setting a specific interface
- vrf: Virtual Routing and Forwarding (VRF) instance name
- Use null for default/global routing table
- global_vrf: Boolean flag indicating if the VRF is global (typically false)

General Notes:
- The `route_maps` array supports defining multiple independent route maps for the device
- Route map entries are evaluated sequentially based on `seq_number`
- At least one routing action (nexthop or interface) should be specified per entry
- VRF and interface/nexthop combinations enable advanced policy-based routing scenarios
- The API performs create or update operations based on existing route map configuration
- All string values are case-sensitive

Policy Integration:
- Route maps work in conjunction with generic policies for policy-based routing
- Generic policies define WHAT traffic to match (source, destination, service criteria)
- Route maps define WHERE to route that traffic (nexthop, interface, VRF)
- Workflow: 1) Create generic policies using POST /topology/generic/policy
2) Reference those policy names in route map matcher_policy_name fields
3) Define routing actions for matched traffic in the route map entries

Returns a list of the topology subnets for all the domains for which the user has permission to access.
This API requires either 'Super admin' or 'Multi-Domain admin' privileges.
For users with 'Super admin' permission, the context parameter is optional. If a context is not specified, the Global context will be used.
For users with 'Multi-Domain' privilege, the context parameter is required.
To get the context parameter, call the /domains/ API and use the id included in the returned domain DTO.
Use the optional name parameter to restrict the results to topology subnet names that match the search criteria provided, as follows:
1. If you provide only a mask, then an exact match search is done on the mask portion of the name
e.g. if name=/2, the results will include 1.2.3.4/2, but not 1.2.3.4/22
2. If you provide only a partial or complete IP address, then a contains search is done in the IPv4 block portion of the name
e.g. name=32, the results will include 192.168.205.32/24 and 55.192.32.22/16, but will not include 55.168.205.5/32
3. If you provide both an IPv4 address (either partial or complete) and a mask, then an exact match search is done
e.g. if name=23.4/2, then the results will include 192.168.23.4/2, but will not include 192.168.23.4/23 or 23.4.192.168/2

Use the optional ip parameter to restrict the results to topology subnets that contain this ip, see example below.

User can use ip or name parameter, not both.
The default pagination is start=0 and count=50.

operations.notes: Fetches rule documentation for a single rule given by revision ID and rule ID.

Modify rule documentation for a single rule identified by revision ID and rule ID.
A single rule can be set as either a stealth rule or legacy rule. If both flags are set, an error will be returned (error 400, Bad request).
If no rule documentation exists for the rule, the specified documentation is added to the rule and the response code is: 201 Created.
If rule documentation already exists for the rule, the specified documentation replaces the existing documentation and the response code is: 204 No Content.
Record set entries that are automatically created or calculated, for example automatic mapping to a SecureChange ticket, cannot be modified.
The following fields are automatically calculated, and cannot be modified:
Permissiveness, Violations, Last Hit, Last Modified, Shadowing Status, Certification Status, Certification Date, Certification Expiration Date, Application Name, Application Owner

Delete rule documentation for a single rule given by revision ID and rule ID.
If the rule has automatic mapping to a ticket, the record is not deleted.
Fetches comment for revision given by revision ID.
Fetches rule documentation for a single rule given by device ID and rule ID

Modify rule documentation for a single rule given by device ID and rule ID
A single rule can be set as either a stealth rule or legacy rule. If both flags are set, an error will be returned (error 400, Bad request).
If there is no existing rule documentation for the rule, the specified documentation is added to the rule and the response code is: 201 Created.
If there is existing rule documentation for the rule, the specified documentation replaces the existing documentation and the response code is: 204 No Content.
Record set entries that are automatically created or calculated, for example automatic mapping to a SecureChange ticket, cannot be modified.
The following fields are automatically calculated, and cannot be modified:
Permissiveness, Violations, Last Hit, Last Modified, Shadowing Status, Certification Status, Certification Date, Certification Expiration Date, Application Name, Application Owner
Delete rule documentation for a single rule given by device ID and rule ID

You can search for a string across all rule fields, or you can search for a combination of specific strings in specific fields.
The text format is for a field is <fieldname>:<text> for example uid:9259f6ee-47a0-4996-a214-ab7edc14a916.
For more information, see Rule Search Syntax.

Returns a list of all of the security rules for the specified revision.
Use add=documentation to retrieve rule documentation.
The is_global parameter is device dependent. For ACL devices, only global rules are returned when set to true. For Check Point R80, only global layers are returned when set to true, and specify a layer name in the subpolicy_name parameter This parameter is ignored for all other vendors. The default value is false.

operations.summary: Get services objects matching specified criteria
operations.notes:
You can search for service objects where the name or comment fields have a specified text string,
or you can search for service objects that have an Port or protocol that matches,
or you can search for service objects by uid.

parameters.name: context
parameters.description: Returns results for the specified domain ID.

parameters.name: start
parameters.description: Returns the results beginning with the specified result number.

parameters.name: count
parameters.description: Returns the specified number of results. If this field is not added or if a number greater than 100 is specified, the query uses "count=100".

parameters.name: filter
parameters.description:
"text" filter returns service objects where the name or comment fields have a specified text string. 
"protocol" filter returns service objects that have a protocol that matches specified IP protocol number.
"port" filter returns service objects that have a port that matches specified port number.
 "uid" filter returns service objects with the specified uid.
 If no filter is specified, the "text" filter is used.

parameters.name: device_id
parameters.description: Returns service objects belonging to the specified device_id.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: (For "text" filter) You can specify "name" to find service objects with the specified text in the name field.

parameters.name: comment
parameters.description: (For "text" filter) You can specify "comment" to find service objects with the specified text in the comment field.

operations.summary: Get policy relevance metrics for traffic
operations.notes:
The response lists all the relevant security groups, tags, relevant instances, and count of unrelated instances for each Amazon VPC in the specified traffic path.
A relevant security group contains at least one instance including either the source or destination IP address.
An unrelated instance is included in the security group but not part of the specified traffic path.
If context is provided, path will be calculated for the specified domain context, otherwise the default domain context is used. context is used only if MSSP mode is enabled. If MSSP mode is disabled context is ignored.
To get the context, call the /domains/ API and use the ID included within the returned domain DTO.

operations.summary: Check if tags are compliant with cloud tag policies
operations.notes: Check if the tags of a cloud resource are compliant with the specified cloud tag policy. Specify the tag policy to validate in the TagPolicyViolationsCheckRequestDTO. The tags of a cloud resource are specified as a json object with the attribute 'tags' at the root level. 'tags' attributes can be a list of tag names or a map including both the tag name and value. If no tags are specified or if the tag is specified incorrectly, The compliance check will treat the resource as if it has no tags. If no cloud tag policy violations are found the API returns an empty violations list.
